why: Egyptian public and private libraries need circulation tracking, deposit management, study-desker booking and a public OPAC page. Lending deposits and child-data privacy rules apply.
operator: The library manager oversees book circulation, membership fees, study-desker bookings and overdue fines. Their day is member check-in, book returns and fine collection.
entities: Library (id, nameAr, nameEn, branchId, address, phone, currency, taxRegistration, openingHours)
Member (id, libraryId, name, phone, encryptedChildData, parentConsent, class, membershipType, joinDate, expiryDate, depositsPiasters)
Book (id, libraryId, isbn, titleAr, titleEn, authorAr, authorEn, category, unitPricePiasters, costPiasters, status, locationShelf)
Borrowing (id, memberId, bookId, borrowedAt, dueDate, returnedAt, finePiasters, status)
StudyDesk (id, libraryId, label, capacity, status, bookedBy, bookedAt, expiresAt)
Staff (id, libraryId, name, phone, role, hourlyRatePiasters, status)
batches: No : library carries no stock or expiry
expiry: Not applicable. Borrowing is time-based not product-based
special: The core structures are the membership with deposits, the borrowing lifecycle, the study-desk booking and the child-data privacy flag. Member data with children (under 18) requires parent consent and minimal fields.
screens: OPAC public page: search books by ISBN, title or author, view availability
Member check-in: scan member card, view active borrowings, due dates
Book checkout: scan book barcode, decrement stock, record borrowing with due date
Study desk booking: available desks, book slot, confirm booking, cancel booking
Return book: scan borrowing record, mark returned, compute fine if overdue
Fine management: unpaid fines per member, receipt print, write-off reason
Staff shift: clock in/out, member load per hour, notes
roles: Owner: everything : book inventory, membership, reports, billing
Librarian: member check-in/out, book check-in/out, fine assessment
Assistant: member registration, study desk booking, fine collection
reports: Active borrowings per day: how many books out, by category
Overdue fines revenue: total unpaid, collected, written off per period
Study desk utilisation: booked hours vs available per day
Member retention: new members, renewals, lapsed members per month
Book circulation by category: which genres are most borrowed
integrations: Barcode scanner for book and member check-in
Esc/POS thermal printer for fine receipts and overdue notices
WhatsApp deep link for overdue notices and membership renewals
onboarding: Library basics: name, branch, address, phone, currency, working hours
Collection: the initial book inventory with ISBN, titles and categories
Membership types: the categories (student, adult, child, family) and deposit amounts
Study desks: the desks available and their capacity
First week plan: register first member, check out first book, book first desk
seed: No sector-specific seed data. The engine provides the membership/borrowing/desk schema and role templates.

tasks.title: Add OPAC public search page
tasks.brief: Build the public search page: search books by ISBN, title or author, view availability status. Done when the page loads and displays matching books from Firestore.
tasks.done: When OPAC search works and displays live book data

tasks.title: Add member check-in with scan
tasks.brief: Build the member check-in screen: scan member card, view active borrowings, due dates. Done when the scan works and displays member data correctly.
tasks.done: When member check-in works with barcode scan and displays data

tasks.title: Add book checkout and check-in screen
tasks.brief: Build the checkout screen: scan book barcode, record borrowing with due date, decrement availability. Done when checkout records borrowing and check-in updates status and computes fines.
tasks.done: When book checkout/check-in works end-to-end with due dates and fines

tasks.title: Add study desk booking screen
tasks.brief: Build the desk booking screen: available desks, book slot, confirm, cancel. Done when a desk can be booked and the booking is saved to Firestore.
tasks.done: When study desk booking works end-to-end

tasks.title: Add fine management screen
tasks.brief: Build the fine screen: unpaid fines per member, receipt print, write-off reason. Done when fines are tracked and receipts print correctly.
tasks.done: When fine management works and receipts print

tasks.title: Add member registration with parent consent for children
tasks.brief: Build the member screen: name, phone, class, membership type, parent consent flag for under-18. Done when the member is saved with consent flag and minimal child data.
tasks.done: When member registration works with parent consent flag

tasks.title: Add overdue fines revenue report
tasks.brief: Build the report showing total unpaid, collected and written-off fines per period. Done when the report pulls live data and displays correct figures.
tasks.done: When fines revenue report pulls live data and displays correctly

tasks.title: Add study desk utilisation report
tasks.brief: Build the report showing booked hours vs available per day. Done when the report computes from Firestore and displays correct utilisation.
tasks.done: When study desk utilisation report computes correctly from live data

tasks.title: Add book circulation by category report
tasks.brief: Build the report showing which genres are most borrowed per period. Done when the report computes from Firestore and displays correct circulation counts.
tasks.done: When book circulation report computes correctly from live data

tasks.title: Add onboarding flow for initial library setup
tasks.brief: Build the onboarding flow: library basics, initial book inventory, membership types, study desks. Done when the flow completes and the library appears with all defaults.
tasks.done: When onboarding flow works end-to-end and library is created

risks: Member data with children (under 18) requires parent consent and minimal fields per PDPL
Encryption key loss makes member records unrecoverable
WhatsApp template rejection if not approved by Meta
Overdue fines that accumulate without a cap can violate consumer protection law
